name: WFNS Subarachnoid Haemorrhage Grade

version.label: Original WFNS (1988)
version.detail: Uses GCS and presence of a major focal deficit. GCS 15 with a focal deficit is not defined in the original scale. The 2015 modified WFNS is a separate entry.

reviewStatus: Content drafted from primary sources; pending independent clinician review before clinical release.
purpose: Grading of aneurysmal subarachnoid haemorrhage based on GCS and focal motor deficit.

inputs.label: Major focal neurological deficit
inputs.help: Commonly interpreted as hemiparesis or aphasia.

states.label: Not defined in original WFNS
states.summary: The original WFNS scale does not define a grade for GCS 15 with a focal deficit.
states.detail: Document GCS and the deficit explicitly. The modified WFNS (2015) grades by GCS alone and would assign Grade I.

states.label: Grade I
states.summary: Good-grade SAH (Grades I–III commonly grouped as good grade).

insights.text: In this GCS range the deficit determines Grade II vs III, the distinction with the most inter-rater variability.
Grade may improve after treatment of hydrocephalus or seizures. Record the timing of grading.

limitations: Grade II vs III separation has limited prognostic discrimination.
confounders: Sedation or intubation (GCS not fully testable)
commonErrors: Using a GCS with a non-testable component.
Counting cranial nerve palsy as a major focal deficit.
doesNotTellYou: Imaging burden or vasospasm risk (see modified Fisher).

sources.citation: Drake CG. Report of World Federation of Neurological Surgeons Committee on a Universal Subarachnoid Hemorrhage Grading Scale. J Neurosurg. 1988;68(6):985-986.
Sano H, Satoh A, Murayama Y, et al. Modified World Federation of Neurosurgical Societies subarachnoid hemorrhage grading system. World Neurosurg. 2015;83(5):801-807.

guide.what: A five-grade SAH scale combining GCS total with the presence of a major focal deficit.
guide.whenUseful: Admission grading, triage communication and research stratification.
guide.howToCalculate: Obtain a full GCS. GCS 15 without deficit = I; 13–14 without deficit = II; 13–14 with deficit = III; 7–12 = IV; 3–6 = V.
guide.clinicalContext: Widely used alongside Hunt & Hess. Grades IV–V are commonly termed poor grade.
